title: Interest Relief for a Late Deficiency Notice — Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail
content:
On a deficiency under a Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract, days after the sale on which the customer had not yet been told of the deficiency carry no interest. The deficiency notice read is the most recent deficiency notice mailed on the contract, and the days are counted in calendar days from the sale date recorded on the contract.

| Deficiency notice on the contract | Interest-free days after the sale |
|---|---|
| No deficiency notice has been mailed | every day after the sale date |
| Most recent notice mailed more than 3 days (the notice grace days) after the sale date | the days after the sale date up to and including the notice mailing date |
| Most recent notice mailed on the sale date or within 3 days after it | none |

The interest-free days are taken off the days after the sale that would otherwise carry interest, never below zero.

### Boundaries (hypothetical)

| Notice mailed | Interest-free days |
|---|---|
| 3 days after the sale date | 0 |
| 4 days after the sale date | 4 |
| 25 days after the sale date | 25 |
| Never | all post-sale days |

Example: a sale on the 2nd of a month and a deficiency notice mailed on the 20th give 18 interest-free days. If the days after the sale carrying interest were 30, 12 remain; if they were 10, none remain, never fewer than zero. The dates and counts are illustrative.
